## BrowserClipboard

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public service BrowserClipboard implements Clipboard
```

The standard [`Clipboard`](#clipboard): the browser's asynchronous clipboard
(`navigator.clipboard`).

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  `true` in a secure context whose browser has the clipboard API; see
  [`Clipboard.isSupported`](#clipboard).
- `@UserAction func write(text: String) async throws ClipboardWriteError`
  Writes `text` with the browser's clipboard; see
  [`Clipboard.write(text:)`](#clipboard).
- `@UserAction func readText() async throws ClipboardReadError -> String?`
  Reads the browser's clipboard as text; see
  [`Clipboard.readText()`](#clipboard).

## BrowserFiles

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public service BrowserFiles implements Files
```

The standard [`Files`](#files): the browser's file picker (an `input` of type
`file`) and downloads through an object URL.

**Members**

- `@UserAction func open(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> File`

- `@UserAction func openAll(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> List<File>`

## Clipboard

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Clipboard
```

Plain text on the system clipboard (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`,
"Clipboard"). A client-only platform interface: [`BrowserClipboard`](#browserclipboard) is
injected with no `use` rule, and [`k.test.TestClipboard`](k-test.md#testclipboard) replaces it in
tests. For the common "copy this" button a view needs no service:
[`CopyButton`](#copybutton) does it.

Both members must be called from a user's action (a click handler)
before its first `await`: browsers allow clipboard access only then.

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  Whether this browser can use the clipboard here: `false` outside a
  secure context (`http:` on a host other than `localhost`), and
  during server rendering. It doesn't change while the page is open.
- `@UserAction func write(text: String) async throws ClipboardWriteError`
  Replaces the clipboard's content with `text`.

  - Throws: [`ClipboardWriteError.unsupported`](#clipboardwriteerror) where
    `isSupported` is `false`, [`ClipboardWriteError.denied`](#clipboardwriteerror) when
    the browser refuses.
- `@UserAction func readText() async throws ClipboardReadError -> String?`
  Reads the clipboard's text. Some browsers show a "Paste"
  confirmation for each read.

  - Returns: the text, or `nil` when the clipboard holds no text (an
    image, or nothing).
  - Throws: [`ClipboardReadError.unsupported`](#clipboardreaderror) where `isSupported`
    is `false`, [`ClipboardReadError.denied`](#clipboardreaderror) when the browser or the
    user refuses.

## ClipboardReadError

```k,ignore
public enum ClipboardReadError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why [`Clipboard.readText()`](#clipboard) read nothing
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Clipboard").

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  This browser or context has no clipboard ([`Clipboard.isSupported`](#clipboard)
  is `false`).
- `case denied`
  The browser or the user refused, which may happen at each read.

```k,ignore
public enum ClipboardWriteError implements Error, Equatable
```

## CopyButton

```k,ignore
public component CopyButton
```

A button that copies `text` to the clipboard
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "CopyButton"):
`CopyButton(text: invite.url, label: "Copy invite link")`.

Its accessible name is `label`. After a copy it shows "Copied" for two
seconds (on the injected [`k.time.Clock`](k-time.md#clock)) and announces it in a polite
live region; the button keeps its size. It uses the injected
[`Clipboard`](#clipboard), so in `k test` it writes to [`k.test.TestClipboard`](k-test.md#testclipboard).
It renders on the server as it will in the browser, and copies once
the page has hydrated.

## File

```k,ignore
public struct File implements Equatable
```

A file the user chose, or one the app made to save
(`docs/design/42-files.md`). A value: its whole content is in `bytes`.

**Members**

- `let name: String`
  The file name, without a path ("board.json").
- `let mediaType: String`
  The media type ("application/json"); empty when the browser doesn't
  know it.
- `let bytes: Bytes`
  The whole content.
- `static var maximumSize: Int`
  The largest file [`Files.open`](#files) reads, in bytes: 16 MiB, 16777216.
- `var text: String?`
  The content as UTF-8 text; `nil` if it isn't valid UTF-8.
- `var size: Int`
  The size of the content, in bytes.
- `static func fromText(name: String, type: FileType, text: String) -> File`
  Makes a file of `text` encoded as UTF-8, to save with
  [`Files.save(_:)`](#files).

  - Parameters:
    - name: the file name, without a path ("board.json").
    - type: the kind of file, which gives its `mediaType`.
    - text: the content.

## FileOpenError

```k,ignore
public enum FileOpenError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why [`Files.open`](#files) or [`Files.openAll`](#files) returned no file
(`docs/design/42-files.md`).

**Members**

- `case cancelled`
  The user closed the picker without choosing a file.
- `case tooLarge(limit: Int)`
  A chosen file is larger than `limit` bytes
  ([`File.maximumSize`](#file)).
- `case unreadable`
  The browser couldn't read a chosen file, or can't show a picker.

## Files

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Files
```

Opening files the user chooses, and saving files the app generates as
downloads (`docs/design/42-files.md`). A client-only platform interface:
[`BrowserFiles`](#browserfiles) is injected with no `use` rule, and
[`k.test.TestFiles`](k-test.md#testfiles) replaces it in tests.

`open(accepting:)` and `openAll(accepting:)` must be called from a
user's action (a click handler) before its first `await`: browsers show
a file picker only in response to one.

**Members**

- `@UserAction func open(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> File`
  Asks the user to choose one file and reads it.

  - Parameter types: the kinds of file offered; any file when empty.
  - Returns: the chosen file, read in full.
  - Throws: [`FileOpenError.cancelled`](#fileopenerror) when the picker is closed
    without a choice, [`FileOpenError.tooLarge`](#fileopenerror) for a file over
    [`File.maximumSize`](#file) and [`FileOpenError.unreadable`](#fileopenerror) when the
    file can't be read.
- `@UserAction func openAll(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> List<File>`
  Asks the user to choose any number of files and reads them.

  - Parameter types: the kinds of file offered; any file when empty.
  - Returns: the chosen files, in the order chosen.
  - Throws: as `open(accepting:)`, for any of the files.
- `func save(_ file: File) throws FileSaveError`
  Saves `file` as a download named after its [`File.name`](#file).

  - Throws: [`FileSaveError.unavailable`](#filesaveerror) when the browser refuses
    downloads.


A kind of file the picker offers (`docs/design/42-files.md`): its media

- `var fileExtension: String`

## Geolocation

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Geolocation
```

The device's position (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`,
"Geolocation"). A client-only platform interface:
[`BrowserGeolocation`](#browsergeolocation) is injected with no `use` rule, and
[`k.test.TestGeolocation`](k-test.md#testgeolocation) replaces it in tests.

Only `requestAccess()` asks the user, and only from a user's action
(a click handler, before its first `await`). Every other member checks
the permission first and never prompts: while it is `.prompt` they
throw [`LocationError.notAsked`](#locationerror).

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  Whether this browser can locate the device here: `false` outside a
  secure context (`http:` on a host other than `localhost`), and
  during server rendering. It doesn't change while the page is open.
- `var permission: PermissionState`
  Whether the app may read the position. Reactive: a view or a
  `@Derived` value that reads it updates when the user changes the
  site's settings. `.prompt` during server rendering.
- `@UserAction func requestAccess() async -> PermissionState`
  Asks the user for access, unless `permission` already says
  `.granted` or `.denied`.

  - Returns: the new permission. A refusal is an answer, not an error.
- `func currentPosition(accuracy: LocationAccuracy = .coarse, maximumAge: Duration = 0.seconds, timeout: Duration = 15.seconds) async throws LocationError -> Position`
  Reads the device's position once.

  - Parameters:
    - accuracy: `.coarse` (a city, fast and light on the battery) or
      `.precise`.
    - maximumAge: accepts a cached position this old; `0.seconds`
      asks for a fresh one.
    - timeout: how long to wait for a fix.
  - Throws: [`LocationError.unsupported`](#locationerror) where `isSupported` is
    `false`, `.notAsked` before `requestAccess()`, `.denied` when
    the user refused, `.unavailable` when the device has no fix and
    `.timeout` when none came in time.
- `func watch(accuracy: LocationAccuracy = .coarse) throws LocationError -> Stream<Position>`
  Follows the device's position: the stream yields the first position
  as soon as there is a fix, then each change. It ends when the
  permission is revoked (`permission` then says why) and when its
  owner is cancelled, which stops the browser's watch.

  - Throws: [`LocationError.unsupported`](#locationerror) where `isSupported` is
    `false`, `.notAsked` or `.denied` when `permission` isn't
    `.granted`.

## LocationAccuracy

```k,ignore
public enum LocationAccuracy implements Equatable
```

How exact a position [`Geolocation`](#geolocation) asks for
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Geolocation").

**Members**

- `case coarse`
  Within a few kilometres: enough for a city's weather or "stores near
  me", faster and lighter on the battery. The default.
- `case precise`
  As exact as the device can tell, from satellites where it has them.

## LocationError

```k,ignore
public enum LocationError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why [`Geolocation`](#geolocation) has no position
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Geolocation").

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  This browser or context can't locate the device.
- `case notAsked`
  The user hasn't been asked yet: call
  [`Geolocation.requestAccess()`](#geolocation) from a user's action first.
- `case denied`
  The user, a browser setting or a policy refused.
- `case unavailable`
  The device has no fix.
- `case timeout`
  No position came within the timeout.

## PermissionState

```k,ignore
public enum PermissionState implements Equatable
```

Whether the app may use a permissioned browser feature
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Permissions"). A permissioned
interface exposes it as a reactive `permission` member; only its
`request…` member shows a prompt, and returns the new state.

**Members**

- `case prompt`
  The next request will ask the user, or the browser can't say.
- `case granted`
  The user allowed it.
- `case denied`
  The user, a browser setting or a policy refused it; only the
  browser's site settings can change it now.

## Position

```k,ignore
public struct Position implements Equatable, Codable
```

Where the device is (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Geolocation"):
plain numbers with their unit in the name.

**Members**

- `let latitude: Double`
  Degrees north of the equator (negative south), WGS 84.
- `let longitude: Double`
  Degrees east of Greenwich (negative west), WGS 84.
- `let accuracyMeters: Double`
  The radius of 95% confidence around the position, in metres.
- `let altitudeMeters: Double?`
  Metres above the WGS 84 ellipsoid, when the device knows it.
- `let headingDegrees: Double?`
  The direction of travel, clockwise from true north; `nil` when not
  moving.
- `let speedMetersPerSecond: Double?`
  The ground speed, when the device knows it.
- `let measuredAt: Date`
  When the position was measured.
- `static func sample(latitude: Double, longitude: Double) -> Position`
  A position for tests: 1 km accuracy, nothing else known, measured
  at the [`k.test.TestClock`](k-test.md#testclock)'s time. It exists only in `k test`.

## Share

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Share
```

The system share sheet (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Web
Share"). A client-only platform interface: [`BrowserShare`](#browsershare) is
injected with no `use` rule, and [`k.test.TestShare`](k-test.md#testshare) replaces it in
tests. For the common "share this" button a view needs no service:
[`ShareButton`](#sharebutton) does it.

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  Whether this browser has a share sheet here: `false` on most desktop
  browsers without one, outside a secure context and during server
  rendering. It doesn't change while the page is open.
- `@UserAction(consuming: true) func share(_ content: ShareContent) async throws ShareError`
  Opens the share sheet with `content` and returns when the user has
  picked a target. It uses up the user's action, so one click shares
  once.

  - Throws: [`ShareError.unsupported`](#shareerror) where `isSupported` is
    `false` or the browser can't share `content`,
    [`ShareError.cancelled`](#shareerror) when the user closes the sheet, and
    [`ShareError.denied`](#shareerror) when a policy refuses.

## ShareButton

```k,ignore
public component ShareButton
```

A button that shares `content` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`,
"ShareButton"): `ShareButton(content: .page(.recipe(id: recipe.id),
title: recipe.title), label: "Share recipe")`.

Where the browser can share it opens the share sheet; where it can't,
it copies the link (or the text) to the clipboard and says "Link
copied" (or "Copied") for two seconds in a polite live region. It
renders the same button either way, so server rendering and hydration
agree. It uses the injected [`Share`](#share) and [`Clipboard`](#clipboard), so in `k test`
it shares to [`k.test.TestShare`](k-test.md#testshare) and copies to
[`k.test.TestClipboard`](k-test.md#testclipboard).

## ShareButtonFailure

```k,ignore
public enum ShareButtonFailure implements Error, Equatable
```

Why a [`ShareButton`](#sharebutton) neither shared nor copied
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "ShareButton"). Closing the share
sheet isn't a failure.

**Members**

- `case denied`
  The browser refused the share or the copy: a policy, or the user's
  action was already used.
- `case unsupported`
  The browser can neither share nor copy here (an insecure context).

## ShareContent

```k,ignore
public struct ShareContent implements Equatable
```

What to share (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Web Share"): a page
of the app, a link or text, with an optional title. Built by
`page(_:title:)`, `link(_:title:)` or `text(_:title:)`, so it
always carries something to share.

**Members**

- `let url: Url?`
  The link, absolute.
- `let text: String?`
  The text.
- `let title: String?`
  The title, which some share targets show.
- `static func page(_ page: Page, title: String? = nil) -> ShareContent`
  A page of the app, made absolute against the page's origin in the
  browser (during server rendering its URL is the page's path).
- `static func link(_ url: Url, title: String? = nil) -> ShareContent`
  A link.
- `static func text(_ text: String, title: String? = nil) -> ShareContent`
  Text.

## ShareError

```k,ignore
public enum ShareError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why [`Share.share(_:)`](#share) didn't share
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Web Share").

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  No share sheet here (desktop Firefox, Chromium on Linux, an insecure
  context), or not for this content.
- `case cancelled`
  The user closed the sheet without choosing a target.
- `case denied`
  A policy refused, or the user's action was already used.

## Subscription

```k,ignore
public class Subscription
```

A running callback subscription, such as a handler listening for
messages from the app's other tabs
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Ownership and lifetime"). Discarding
one returned inside an [`k.core.Effect`](k-core.md#effect) is a warning, as for a
[`k.time.TimerHandle`](k-time.md#timerhandle).

**Members**

- `func cancel()`
  Stops the callbacks; cancelling a cancelled subscription does
  nothing.

## TabChannel

```k,ignore
public struct TabChannel<T> where T implements Codable
```

A channel between the app's tabs, paired with the type of its messages:
`TabChannel<CartChange> = TabChannel(name: "cart")`
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Messages between tabs"). A tab
can't post one type and another read a different one: channels with
the same name must carry the same message type.

**Members**

- `init(name: String)`
  Creates the channel named `name`.

  - Parameter name: a string literal; channels with the same name are
    the same channel.
- `var name: String`
  The channel's name.
